newsitem.title: USA: NYC comptroller delays briefing on Swiss banks.
newsitem.headline: NYC comptroller delays briefing on Swiss banks.

text.p: New York City's Comptroller delayed until Wednesday a briefing on his talks in Switzerland with three Swiss banks, Swiss government officials and leaders of the Swiss Jewish community, a spokesman said Tuesday.

Alan Hevesi, the city comptroller, last year asked the banks to explain how they were responding to probes into whether the banks blocked victims of the Holocaust and their survivors from withdrawing valuables deposited in Switzerland for safe-keeping.

The briefing was delayed by one day to allow a senior official from the World Jewish Congress and the leader of an organization for the surivors of Holocaust victims to attend, the comptroller's spokesman said.

Hevesi is a trustee and investment advisor to the city's $70 billion pension fund, which owns stock in the three Swiss banks he met with: Credit Suisse Group, Swiss Bank Corp, and Union Bank of Switzerland. The banks also handle invesments for the city and pension funds.

The New York City Council, which considered whether to require the city's pensions to divest themselves of Swiss banks' stocks, put the proposal on hold after the Swiss government in February created a fund for Holocaust victims.

As of Dec 31, 1996, the city's pensions owned 262,800 shares of Credit Suisse, valued at nearly $26 million, 56,700 shares of Swiss Bank, which were worth almost $10.8 million, and 22,800 shares of Union Bank, which were pegged at about $13.3 million.
